text: move 235 (merging), D4a-02: branch F34 named at the fourth order, key add-condition:P02:T4-006, 22 members (read from the level matrix by d4_cut.py). Name: the design sized to the hands: scale and detail conditioned on crew, upkeep, space and colours. What it changes: P02 says the room settles what its mark will show. In these rooms the design is conditioned by what the room can build and keep: its scale and detail depend on the crew it can assemble, the upkeep it can sustain, the space it can protect and the colours available. Ground: keys.

move 236 (merging), D4a-02: branch F35 named at the third order, key add-step:P01:T3-002, 18 members (read from the level matrix by d4_cut.py). Name: the call made workable: answers ask for a task, and callers supply it. What it changes: P01 says the room calls members and kindred subs to place. In these rooms answering a call is an exchange: a willing member asks what to do, where to start or for backup, and the caller supplies instructions, location cues and visibility (a sticky, other venues), reaching people beyond the room. Ground: keys.

Volume check (out/_analysis/d4a03_volume.py, 2,000 draws, seed 0; concepts per room from the comparison's own counts): the clusters split the rooms by size (eta squared of log concepts 0.255, null maximum 0.026, percentile 100; IT holds 137 of the 176 rooms of the smallest quartile, VA and CH mostly the two largest quartiles); branch membership leans to larger rooms (in a branch Q1 63, Q4 142; in no branch Q1 113, Q4 33), and 11 of 35 branches have a median room size at or above the 95th percentile, none at or below the 5th. Reading: the canvas percentiles of branches and clusters follow room size, so no difference in what rooms kept can be read as independent of size; a large room holds more lines, more keys, and more chances to share one.
